questions.q: Describe the major types of natural vegetation found in India.
answer: India's natural vegetation varies with relief and climate, giving several distinct types.

answer.text: In areas of heavy rainfall, above 200 cm, such as the Western Ghats and the north-east, these dense forests stay green all year and yield rosewood, ebony and mahogany.
The most widespread type, growing in monsoon regions; the trees, such as teak and sal, shed their leaves in the dry season.
Thorn forests and scrub, with acacia and cactus, grow in arid areas like Rajasthan, while montane forests change with altitude in the mountains.
In deltas and coastal areas, salt-tolerant mangroves such as the Sundari trees of the Sundarbans flourish.

questions.q: Why is the conservation of wildlife important, and how is it done in India?
answer: India is a mega-biodiversity country with rich flora and fauna, but many species are threatened by hunting, habitat loss and pollution.

answer.text: Wildlife maintains the balance of nature, supports ecosystems, and is part of our natural heritage; the loss of one species can disturb entire food chains.

India protects wildlife through national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves. Special projects such as Project Tiger, launched in 1973, and Project Elephant protect flagship species. Eighteen biosphere reserves, several recognised by UNESCO, conserve whole ecosystems, and the Botanical and Zoological Surveys study and record species.

answer: Together these efforts help safeguard India's biodiversity for the future.

questions.q: What is biodiversity, and why is India considered a country rich in biodiversity?

answer.text: is the variety of plant and animal life in a region, and India is one of the world's biodiversity-rich countries.
